messages:
alex: Heads up - deploy-bot just moved the canary to eu-west-2 at 10%. I'm seeing a P99 tail spike in the dashboard, can we quick-check?

deploy-bot: deploy started: v2026.03.21-canary -> service/inference-eu (traffic=10%) by alex. Instance groups: inference-eu-1 (g4dn). Logs: https://deploys/redwood/1758889991

maya: on it, pulling metrics now. which panel are you looking at?

alex: the latency panel (per-route p99). tail jumped from 180ms -> 1.2s around 1758889950.

sre_oncall: seeing the same on traces. a few requests have KV cache miss patterns and high GPU scheduling wait.

ops_lead: can we pin the canary to the old model variant while we investigate? avoid broader rollout.

jen: what about backing the traffic down to 0% and rollback to previous version? need quick consensus.

liam: if it's KV cache related, rolling back the model may not help; it could be an infra scheduling regression from the new runtime flags. do we have rollout flags?

maya: check: runtime flag --enable-continuous-batching was toggled in this release. that could increase kernel contention under short sequences.

alex: proposal: STOP the rollout, pin traffic at 0% for eu, open an infra rollback vs model rollback decision tree. who can give go/no-go within 10m?

sre_oncall: +1 stop. I'll open an alert runbook and capture traces. recommend pin traffic and keep instances up for logs.

ops_lead: vote: stop and pin -> rollback infra flag if investigation shows contention.

jen: vote: stop & pin. prepped rollback playbook for model and for runtime flag.

liam: vote: stop. I'll collect the GPU sched/fs metrics and confirm whether it's the batching flag.

deploy-bot: action: traffic update requested by alex. setting traffic for v2026.03.21-canary -> 0% in eu-west-2. (request_id=rb-1758889991-01)

maya: confirmed - traffic now at 0% for canary, baseline remains v2026.03.18-stable.

alex: thanks. ops_lead, please indicate if you want an immediate infra rollback or further data first.

ops_lead: prefer to validate traces first (5-10m). if we see kernel contention across >60% of affected spans, rollback runtime flag. else fall back to model rollback.

jen: I'll stage the runtime-flag rollback patch on the canary infra group; ready to flip if SRE confirms. commands ready:```kubectl patch cm infra-flags -n inference --patch '{"data":{"enable-continuous-batching":"false"}}'```

liam: digging logs now. initial signal shows busy_wait spikes and small KV cache evictions correlating with high p99. looks like batching increases scheduling pressure for short requests.

sre_oncall: concur. evidence leans infra flag. ops_lead, recommend rolling the flag back on canary infra, keep model pinned.

ops_lead: agree, proceed with infra flag rollback on canary only. jen, schedule the patch and coordinate with deploy bot to monitor.

jen: applying patch to canary infra group now. will watch metrics.

deploy-bot: note: patch applied to infra config (infra-flags) for inference-eu-1. monitor window 5m.

maya: metrics trending down — p99 dropping back towards baseline after ~70s.

alex: good to hear. keep canary traffic at 0% for now. ops_lead, after 10m of stability do we want to attempt a limited re-release at 5% without the batching flag?

ops_lead: yes, if stability holds for 10m, re-run canary at 5% with flag disabled and observe. jen, coordinate the traffic ramp when ready.

liam: logging note: capture heap and kernel timers for the next 15m, and tag traces with rollout_id=1758889991.

jen: ready to bump to 5% on command.

alex: ok, consensus = STOP -> pin -> infra-flag rollback on canary -> reattempt 5% after 10m stable. I'll update release notes and changelog with the incident note.

deploy-bot: incident note attached to deploy run: "canary halted - p99 tail spike; infra flag rollback applied to canary; awaiting stability window". run_id=1758889991

maya: adding a short blurb to release-notes draft: "Temporarily disabled continuous batching in EU canary due to transient latency tail. Investigating performance implications before broader rollout."

alex: thanks all. we'll reconvene if anything changes. :thumbsup:
